questions.q: The superior parathyroid gland originates from:
questions.exp: Superior parathyroid: 4th pharyngeal pouch. (Book p111)

questions.q: The location of the superior parathyroid gland is:
opts: Constant: posterior aspect of thyroid lobe
Constant: anterior aspect of thyroid lobe
questions.exp: Superior parathyroid location constant: posterior aspect of thyroid lobe. (Book p111)

questions.q: The inferior parathyroid gland originates from:
questions.exp: Inferior parathyroid: 3rd pharyngeal pouch; location variable. (Book p111)

questions.q: The thymus is also derived from the 3rd pharyngeal pouch; therefore in parathyroid surgery the thymus is removed along with the:
questions.exp: Thymus also from 3rd pouch - removed along with inf. parathyroid gland in parathyroid Sx → ↑ yield. (Book p111)

questions.q: What percentage of people have 5 parathyroid glands?
questions.exp: 5% have 5 parathyroid glands. (Book p111)

questions.q: Parathyroid glands are identified intraoperatively by the:
questions.exp: Identification: sentinel pad of fat (golden yellow). (Book p111)

questions.q: On touch, the parathyroid gland:
questions.exp: Turns dusky on touch. (Book p111)

questions.q: The half-life of PTH and its function are:
questions.exp: Secretes parathyroid hormones (PTH), T 1/2: 5-7 mins; function: ↑ plasma Ca2+ concentration. (Book p111)

questions.q: The mnemonic for clinical features of hyperparathyroidism is:
opts: Bones, stones, abdominal groans, psychiatric overtones
Stones, bones, groans and moans only
questions.exp: Mnemonic: Bones, stones, abdominal groans, psychiatric overtones. (Book p111)

questions.q: Which fracture pattern is part of the 'bones' of hyperparathyroidism?
questions.exp: Bones: pathological fracture, subperiosteal resorption, salt & pepper skull, brown tumors. (Book p111)

questions.q: Subperiosteal bone resorption in hyperparathyroidism is m/c in the:
questions.exp: Subperiosteal bone resorption: m/c in radial aspect. (Book p111)

questions.q: The 'salt & pepper' appearance of hyperparathyroidism is seen in the:
questions.exp: Salt & pepper skull. (Book p111)

questions.q: Brown tumors of hyperparathyroidism are also known as:
opts: Osteitis fibrosa cystica / von Recklinghausen disease of bone
questions.exp: Brown tumors: osteitis fibrosa cystica / von Recklinghausen disease of bone. (Book p111)

questions.q: Renal stones in hyperparathyroidism are typically:
questions.exp: Stones: recurrent & multiple renal stones (m/c). (Book p112)

questions.q: The m/c renal stone in hyperparathyroidism, which is radiopaque, is:
questions.exp: Calcium oxalate stone: renal stones (m/c) → radiopaque. (Book p112)

questions.q: The 'abdominal groans' of hyperparathyroidism include abdominal colic and:
questions.exp: Abdominal groans: abdominal colic, pancreatitis. (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: The m/c cause of primary hyperparathyroidism is:
questions.exp: Adenoma >> hyperplasia. (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: In primary hyperparathyroidism, adenoma versus hyperplasia means:
opts: Enlargement of 1 gland vs all 4 glands
questions.exp: Adenoma: enlargement of 1 gland; hyperplasia: enlargement of all 4 glands. (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: Risk factors for primary hyperparathyroidism are radiation exposure and:
questions.exp: Risk factors: 1. Radiation exposure 2. MEN syndrome (MEN1, 2A). (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: MEN-syndrome-associated hyperparathyroidism is a familial syndrome showing:
questions.exp: Familial syndrome; multiglandular disease (adenoma > hyperplasia). (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: The biochemical profile of primary hyperparathyroidism is:
opts: ↑ PTH, ↑ S. Ca2+, ↓ S. phosphorous, ↑ calcitriol
questions.exp: ↑ PTH; ↑ S. Ca2+ (total & ionised); ↑ U. Ca2+ & phosphate; ↓ S. phosphorous; ↑ calcitriol. (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: The IOC investigation for a parathyroid adenoma is:
questions.exp: Tc99m sestamibi scan: IOC (USG neck also part of workup). (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: Tc99 localises in a PTH adenoma because the adenoma is rich in:
questions.exp: Tc99 localises in PTH adenoma (rich in mitochondria). (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: A false positive on sestamibi scan is:
questions.exp: False positive: Warthin tumour (rich in mitochondria). (Book p112)

questions.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
questions.q: SPECT, the m/c type of sestamibi imaging, stands for:
questions.exp: Types: single isotope dual phase; dual isotope subtraction imaging; SPECT: Single Photon Emission CT (m/c). (Book p112)

questions.sec: Localisation of Adenoma & Mx of Adenoma
questions.q: Concordant imaging on sestamibi scan & USG leads to:
opts: Pre-op marking with USG → minimally invasive parathyroidectomy (MIP)
questions.exp: Concordant imaging → pre-op marking with USG → minimally invasive parathyroidectomy (MIP). (Book p113)

questions.sec: Localisation of Adenoma & Mx of Adenoma
questions.q: Discordant imaging on sestamibi scan & USG is followed by:
questions.exp: Discordant imaging → 4D CT → 4 gland exploration or pre-op marking with USG and MIP. (Book p113)

questions.sec: Localisation of Adenoma & Mx of Adenoma
questions.q: Management of a parathyroid adenoma is:
opts: Removal of adenomatous gland (MIP or open removal)
questions.exp: Mx of adenoma: removal of adenomatous gland - minimally invasive parathyroidectomy (MIP) or open removal. (Book p113)

questions.sec: Localisation of Adenoma & Mx of Adenoma
questions.q: Steps to ensure correct gland removal in MIP are pre-op marking with USG and the:
questions.exp: Steps: 1. Pre-op marking with USG 2. Miami protocol. (Book p113)

questions.sec: Localisation of Adenoma & Mx of Adenoma
questions.q: In the Miami protocol, success is confirmed when the PTH level 10-15 mins after gland removal falls by:
questions.exp: Miami protocol: pre-op PTH level → 10-15 mins after gland removal → ↓ PTH by > 50%. (Book p113)

questions.q: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) for parathyroid hyperplasia is indicated in:
opts: Multigland disease, familial syndromes, lithium induced
questions.exp: MIS for hyperplasia: C/I - multigland disease, familial syndromes, lithium induced. (Book p113)

questions.q: In subtotal parathyroidectomy for hyperplasia:
opts: 3½ glands removed, ½ gland retained in neck
questions.exp: 3½ glands removed, ½ gland retained in neck; disadvantage: Sx difficult in recurrence d/t fibrosis. (Book p113)

questions.q: In total parathyroidectomy with autotransplantation, ½ gland is placed in the:
questions.exp: 4 glands removed; ½ gland autotransplanted in brachioradialis (of non-dominant hand); advantage: easy removal in recurrence. (Book p113)

questions.q: Thymectomy during parathyroid surgery is indicated for:
opts: Involvement of lower PTH glands, 2° hyperparathyroidism, familial syndromes
questions.exp: Thymectomy indication: involvement of lower PTH gland, 2° hyperparathyroidism, familial syndromes. (Book p113)

questions.q: Why is the PTH gland NOT transplanted into the sternocleidomastoid?
questions.exp: Note: transplantation of PTH gland in sternocleidomastoid → injury to gland during thyroidectomy. (Book p114)

questions.q: Indications for Sx in asymptomatic hyperparathyroidism include serum calcium:
questions.exp: S. calcium > 1 mg/dl above reference range. (Book p114)

questions.q: Which complication lists as an indication for Sx in asymptomatic hyperparathyroidism?
questions.exp: Complications: e.g. nephrolithiasis; life threatening hypercalcemic episode. (Book p114)

questions.q: Severe hypercalciuria indicating surgery in asymptomatic disease is:
questions.exp: Severe hypercalciuria (> 400 mg/24 hrs). (Book p114)

questions.q: Other indications for Sx in asymptomatic hyperparathyroidism are:
questions.exp: ↓ bone mass: osteoporosis; age < 50 yrs. (Book p114)

questions.q: Residual hyperparathyroidism is defined as ↑ PTH:
questions.exp: Residual hyperPTH: ↑ PTH within 6 weeks. (Book p114)

questions.q: Recurrent hyperparathyroidism is defined as ↑ PTH:
questions.exp: Recurrent hyperPTH: ↑ PTH 6 months after normalisation. (Book p114)

questions.q: The Casanova test measures PTH in neck & arm veins; recurrence is positive when:
opts: Arm vein PTH = 20 × neck vein PTH
Neck vein PTH equals arm vein PTH
Arm vein PTH = half of neck vein PTH
questions.exp: Casanova test: measures PTH in neck & arm veins; arm vein PTH = 20 × neck vein PTH → recurrence +ve → removal of gland. (Book p114)

questions.q: Hungry bone syndrome after PTH gland removal is:
questions.exp: Hungry bone syndrome: post PTH gland removal → Ca2+ influx into bones → hypocalcemia. (Book p114)

questions.q: Hypercalcemic crisis is seen in:
questions.exp: Seen in 1° hyperparathyroidism & hypercalcemia of malignancy (paraneoplastic). (Book p114)

questions.q: Hypercalcemia of malignancy (paraneoplastic) in hypercalcemic crisis is classically seen with:
opts: Squamous cell cancer, breast cancer, prostate cancer
questions.exp: Hypercalcemia of malignancy (paraneoplastic syndrome): squamous cell cancer, breast cancer, prostate cancer. (Book p114)

questions.q: Hypercalcemic crisis is a medical emergency defined by Ca2+:
questions.exp: Ca2+ > 14 mg/dl. (Book p114)

questions.q: Symptoms of hypercalcemic crisis include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Symptoms: confusion, nausea & vomiting, anuria, dehydration, abdominal pain. (Book p114)

questions.q: ECG changes in hypercalcemic crisis are:
questions.exp: ECG changes: ↑ PR interval, ↓ QT interval, arrhythmia. (Book p114)

questions.q: Ca2+ above what level causes cardiac arrest in hypercalcemic crisis?
questions.exp: Ca2+ > 16 mg/dl → cardiac arrest. (Book p114)

questions.q: The first step in management of hypercalcemic crisis is:
questions.exp: Aggressive IV fluid therapy: first step. (Book p114)

questions.q: The diuretic used in hypercalcemic crisis management is:
questions.exp: Diuretics: furosemide. (Book p114)

questions.q: Bisphosphonates in hypercalcemic crisis (if RFT & urine output normal) act on the:
questions.exp: Bisphosphonates if RFT & urine output are normal; acts on osteoclast; calcitonin added if zoledronic acid/denosumab is given. (Book p114)

questions.q: Dialysis in hypercalcemic crisis is reserved for:
questions.exp: Dialysis: if failure of other methods. (Book p114)

questions.q: Secondary hyperparathyroidism is associated with:
questions.exp: Associated with PTH hyperplasia. (Book p115)

questions.q: The m/c cause of secondary hyperparathyroidism is:
questions.exp: Chronic renal failure (m/c). (Book p115)

questions.q: In chronic renal failure, secondary hyperparathyroidism develops because of:
opts: Failure of hydroxylation of vit D → ↓ vit D3 / ↓ S. Ca2+ → PTH hyperplasia
questions.exp: Failure of hydroxylation of vit D → ↓ vit D3 / ↓ S. Ca2+ → PTH hyperplasia; reversible cause of 2° hyperPTH. (Book p115)

questions.q: Other causes of secondary hyperparathyroidism include defective intestinal absorption, vit D3 deficiency and:
questions.exp: Causes: defective intestinal absorption, lithium intake, vit D3 deficiency. (Book p115)

questions.q: Investigations in secondary hyperparathyroidism show:
opts: N/↓ S. Ca, ↑ S. phosphorous, ↓ calcitriol, ↑ PTH
questions.exp: N/↓ S. Ca (total & ionized); ↑ S. phosphorous; ↓ calcitriol; ↑ PTH. (Book p115)

questions.q: The mainstay of treatment of secondary hyperparathyroidism is:
questions.exp: Correction of chronic renal failure; renal transplantation: mainstay of Rx. (Book p115)

questions.q: The calcimimetic used in secondary hyperparathyroidism is:
questions.exp: Cinacalcet: calcimimetics - acts on Ca2+ sensing receptors; ↓ requirement of Sx. (Book p115)

questions.q: Which is TRUE for secondary hyperparathyroidism?
opts: No localisation of gland is required; surgery = mx of hyperplasia
questions.exp: No localisation of gland required; surgery: mx of hyperplasia; also vit D3 supplementation & low phosphate diet. (Book p115)

questions.q: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism is:
opts: Persistent autonomous hypercalcemic hyperPTH post kidney transplant
questions.exp: Causes: persistent autonomous hypercalcemic hyperPTH post kidney transplant. (Book p115)

questions.q: Investigations in tertiary hyperparathyroidism show:
opts: ↑ PTH, ↑ S. Ca2+, ↓ S. phosphate; USG neck confirms nodular enlargement
questions.exp: ↑ PTH; ↑ S. Ca2+; ↓ S. phosphate; USG neck: confirms nodular enlargement. (Book p115)

questions.q: Treatment of tertiary hyperparathyroidism is:
opts: Subtotal parathyroidectomy (mainstay) or embolisation of gland
questions.exp: Subtotal parathyroidectomy (mainstay); embolisation of gland. (Book p115)

questions.q: Calciphylaxis (hypercalcemic uremic arteriopathy) is seen in:
questions.exp: Seen in chronic dialysis; hypercalcemic uremic arteriopathy. (Book p115)

questions.q: Calciphylaxis causes Ca2+ deposition in skin, blood vessels & soft tissues leading to:
opts: Gangrene, painful purpura, calcification in breast
questions.exp: Ca2+ deposition → a. gangrene b. painful purpura c. calcification in breast. (Book p115)

questions.q: Pseudohyperparathyroidism (AKA hypercalcemia of malignancy) is a:
questions.exp: AKA hypercalcemia of malignancy; paraneoplastic syndrome; PTH related peptide (PTHrp) mediated. (Book p116)

questions.q: Pseudohyperparathyroidism is m/c seen in:
questions.exp: Seen in squamous cell carcinoma of lung (m/c), breast cancer, prostate cancer. (Book p116)

questions.q: Investigations in pseudohyperparathyroidism show:
opts: ↑ S. Ca, normal S. phosphorous, N/↓ calcitriol & PTH, ↑ PTHrp
questions.exp: ↑ S. Ca; normal S. phosphorous; N/↓ calcitriol, PTH; ↑ PTHrp. (Book p116)

questions.q: Management of pseudohyperparathyroidism is:
questions.exp: Same as hypercalcemic crisis. (Book p116)

questions.q: Risk factors for parathyroid cancer are:
questions.exp: Risk factors: radiation exposure; HRPT2 gene. (Book p116)

questions.q: HPE of parathyroid cancer shows fibrous bands & vascular invasion; IHC shows inactivation of:
questions.exp: HPE: fibrous bands & vascular invasion; IHC: inactivation of parafibromin. (Book p116)

questions.q: The m/c cause of death in parathyroid cancer is:
questions.exp: Features of hypercalcemia; hypercalcemic crisis (arrhythmia): m/c cause of death. (Book p116)

questions.q: Management of parathyroid cancer is:
opts: Surgery: R0 resection (microscopic clearance); octreotide & cinacalcet ↓ symptoms
questions.exp: Surgery: R0 resection (microscopic clearance); octreotide, cinacalcet → ↓ symptoms. (Book p116)

questions.q: The m/c cause of hypoparathyroidism is:
questions.exp: 1. Iatrogenic (m/c) 2. DiGeorge syndrome. (Book p116)

questions.q: DiGeorge syndrome (mnemonic CATCH 22) is caused by:
questions.exp: Deletion of 22q11. (Book p116)

questions.q: The 'H' in the CATCH 22 mnemonic of DiGeorge syndrome stands for:
questions.exp: CATCH 22: Cardiac anomalies, Atypical facies, Thymic hypoplasia, Cleft lip & palate, Hypocalcemia; 22 = deletion 22q11. (Book p116)

units.title: Surgical Anatomy & Physiology
units.guide: Superior parathyroid from 4th pouch (constant, posterior thyroid), inferior from 3rd pouch (variable) like the thymus - so thymus goes with the inferior gland to ↑ yield; 5% have 5 glands. Identify by the golden-yellow sentinel fat pad (turns dusky on touch); PTH (t½ 5-7 mins) raises plasma Ca2+.

units.title: Clinical Features of Hyperparathyroidism
units.guide: Bones, stones, abdominal groans, psychiatric overtones: pathological fractures, subperiosteal resorption m/c radial side, salt & pepper skull, brown tumor = osteitis fibrosa cystica (von Recklinghausen bone disease); recurrent multiple radiopaque calcium-oxalate renal stones; colic & pancreatitis.

units.title: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation
units.sec: Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Causes, Risk Factors & Investigation · p112
units.guide: Adenoma (1 gland) >> hyperplasia (4 glands); risks radiation & MEN1/2A (familial, multiglandular). Biochem: ↑PTH, ↑S.Ca, ↑U.Ca/phosphate, ↓S.phosphate, ↑calcitriol. Sestamibi = IOC (Tc99 sticks to mitochondria-rich adenoma; Warthin tumor false +); SPECT = Single Photon Emission CT m/c.

units.title: Localisation of Adenoma & Mx of Adenoma
units.sec: Localisation of Adenoma & Mx of Adenoma · p113
units.guide: Concordant sestamibi+USG → USG-marked MIP; discordant → 4D CT → 4-gland exploration or USG-marked MIP. Adenoma mx = remove the gland (MIP/open); correct gland ensured by USG marking + Miami protocol (PTH ↓ >50% at 10-15 min post-removal).

units.title: Management of Hyperplasia & Thymectomy
units.guide: Hyperplasia MIS for multigland/familial/lithium: subtotal 3½ removed (½ in neck, but recurrence Sx hard d/t fibrosis) or total + ½ autotransplant in non-dominant brachioradialis (easy re-excision). Thymectomy for lower-gland involvement, 2° hyperPTH, familial; never implant into sternocleidomastoid - thyroidectomy would injure it.

units.title: Sx in Asymptomatic Hyperparathyroidism & Complications
units.sec: Sx in Asymptomatic Hyperparathyroidism & Complications · p114
units.guide: Asymptomatic Sx if S.Ca >1 above reference, nephrolithiasis/life-threatening episode, hypercalciuria >400mg/24h, osteoporosis, age <50. Residual = ↑PTH within 6 wks; recurrent = ↑PTH 6 months after normal (Casanova neck/arm vein test, +ve → remove gland). Hungry bone: Ca2+ floods into bones → hypocalcemia.

units.title: Hypercalcemic Crisis
units.guide: Emergency at Ca >14 (arrest >16) in 1° hyperPTH or malignancy (squamous lung, breast, prostate). Confusion, vomiting, anuria, dehydration, abdominal pain; ECG ↑PR ↓QT arrhythmia. Rx: aggressive IV fluids first, furosemide, bisphosphonates (osteoclast) + calcitonin, dialysis if all fail.

units.title: Secondary Hyperparathyroidism
units.guide: 2° = PTH hyperplasia from chronic renal failure (m/c: failed vit D hydroxylation → ↓D3/↓Ca), malabsorption, lithium, D3 deficiency. N/↓ Ca, ↑ phosphate, ↓ calcitriol, ↑ PTH. Rx: fix CRF (renal transplant mainstay), D3, low-phosphate diet, cinacalcet (calcimimetic on Ca-sensing receptor); no localisation needed, surgery treats hyperplasia.

units.title: Tertiary Hyperparathyroidism
units.guide: Tertiary = persistent autonomous hypercalcemic hyperPTH after kidney transplant: ↑PTH, ↑Ca, ↓ phosphate, nodular glands on USG. Rx subtotal parathyroidectomy (mainstay) or gland embolisation.

units.title: Miscellaneous: Calciphylaxis
units.guide: Calciphylaxis in chronic dialysis: hypercalcemic uremic arteriopathy - Ca2+ deposits in skin/vessels/soft tissue → gangrene, painful purpura, breast calcification.

units.title: Pseudohyperparathyroidism
units.guide: Pseudohyperparathyroidism = hypercalcemia of malignancy, PTHrp-mediated paraneoplastic (squamous lung m/c, breast, prostate): ↑Ca, normal phosphate, N/↓ PTH & calcitriol, ↑PTHrp; treat like hypercalcemic crisis.

units.title: Parathyroid Cancer
units.guide: Rare cancer: radiation & HRPT2 risks; HPE fibrous bands + vascular invasion, IHC parafibromin inactivation. Death m/c from hypercalcemic crisis arrhythmia; Rx R0 resection, octreotide/cinacalcet for symptoms.

units.title: Hypoparathyroidism & DiGeorge Syndrome
units.guide: Hypoparathyroidism: iatrogenic m/c then DiGeorge (CATCH 22 = 22q11 deletion: Cardiac anomalies, Atypical facies, Thymic hypoplasia, Cleft lip/palate, Hypocalcemia).
